plans.note: Cap is mutual at greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000 with Excluded Claims defined in 21.3; check adequacy of the cap multiple for a health-data hosting deal and that data/security, privacy and indemnity carve-outs are uncapped (21.3 appears to cover them). Note 21.3 cross-refers to indemnification obligations that may sit in a missing Section 20.

No Section 20 (indemnities) appears in the outline, yet Section 9.3 cross-references 'the remedies required by Section 20.5' and 19.5/21.3 assume indemnity obligations exist. Flag the missing Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity and confirm no broad Customer indemnity is inserted.

Second 12.4 imposes a 24-month, worldwide, all-territory non-compete on Customer — directly contrary to playbook; it also contradicts 12.3, which disclaims any non-compete. Target deletion and rely on 12.3.
First 7.2 conditions engaging another provider on a disclose-and-match obligation, functioning as a de facto exclusivity gate; 12.3 preserves supplier freedom and should control.
First 7.2 is a reverse MFN running against us (we must disclose and match third-party offers). Wrong direction; delete, and note 12.3's disclaimer of any most-favoured-customer commitment.

First 12.4 bars soliciting, hiring or employing any Vendor employee for 24 months 'regardless of how the employee applies' — no general-advertising carve-out and one-sided. Narrow to 12 months, non-solicitation only, with general-recruitment carve-out consistent with 12.3.

Section 9 contains only breach, insolvency and cause-based rights (9.4 is absent from the outline); no Customer termination for convenience. Compounded by 2.1's take-or-pay with 'no reduction or termination rights'.

8.2 gives a 30-day non-renewal window with a 60-day reminder backstop and 8.3 caps uplifts at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice — largely compliant; verify the notice window and that increases cannot apply to prepaid periods.
28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction (outside accepted list) and conflicts with 28.2's New York County exclusive jurisdiction; resolve to New York law and New York courts.

24.1–24.4 already permit our affiliate/successor assignment and bar Vendor from repricing or terminating on our change of control; confirm 24.3's residual consent requirement does not swallow 24.1 and that 13.3 licence transfer tracks Section 24.

14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of Deliverables we pay for plus only a revocable, non-transferable term licence — contrary to playbook and inconsistent with 13.2/14.3. 14.1 correctly preserves our ownership of Customer Data; check 1.3/1.4 exclusions and 15.1 no-training language.

13.1–13.2 cover Affiliates and contractors and give a perpetual paid-up licence, but 14.2 makes the Deliverable licence revocable and non-transferable; align 14.2 with 13.2/13.3 so no licence is revocable at will.

22.1–22.3 already limit audits to once yearly with 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, Vendor-borne cost subject to a 5% underpayment shift; confirm the shortfall threshold and confidentiality of findings are acceptable.

No liquidated damages or penalty payable by us appears in the body; service credits are only referenced in 1.5 and any service-level exhibit under 2.2. Confirm the SLA exhibit contains credits in our favour and no penalties, and that 2.1's take-or-pay is not a disguised penalty.

19.1–19.4 give conformity warranties (90 days for Deliverables, term-long for hosted Services) with repair/re-perform then refund and termination; check the 90-day period is adequate and that 19.5's disclaimer does not erode express warranties.
Insurance is present with CGL, WC/EL, E&O and USD 5,000,000 cyber cover plus certificate and non-limitation language; verify limits against health-data exposure and the one-year tail.
2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 per-year, three-year take-or-pay expressly 'without reduction or termination rights' — unacceptable; it also contradicts 12.3's disclaimer of minimum-volume commitments.

Section 10 addresses access cut-off, Deliverable delivery and refunds but contains no transition-assistance or Customer Data extraction/return obligation; note that 16.5 cross-refers to a Section 11 on Customer Data that does not appear in the outline.
